question: A developer wants their project's CLAUDE.md to mention the path to a git workflow guide without pulling its contents into every session's context. They write ` @docs/git-instructions.md ` wrapped in backticks inside a paragraph. What happens when Claude Code parses this CLAUDE.md at session start?
options: A) Claude Code imports the file but truncates it to just the first paragraph, since backticked references are treated as partial-preview imports only.
B) Claude Code still imports the file, because the @ import syntax is resolved before Markdown code span parsing removes the surrounding backticks.
C) Claude Code treats the backtick-wrapped path as literal text and skips the import, since import parsing skips code spans and fenced code blocks.
D) Claude Code raises a parse error and refuses to load the rest of the CLAUDE.md file until the ambiguous backticked reference is removed entirely.
correct_answers: C) Claude Code treats the backtick-wrapped path as literal text and skips the import, since import parsing skips code spans and fenced code blocks.
explanations: Incorrect. There is no partial-preview import behavior; backticked text is either imported in full (outside code spans) or left literal (inside them).
Incorrect. Code span skipping happens during import parsing itself, so the backticks do prevent the import rather than being processed afterward.
Correct. Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks, so wrapping a path in backticks keeps it as literal text instead of triggering an import.
Incorrect. A backticked reference is simply left as literal text; it does not cause a parse error or block loading the rest of the file.
